notes: Official sources could not be opened: textbooksonline.tn.nic.in and e-learn.tnschools.gov.in refuse automated fetching via robots.txt, tnschools.gov.in and scert.tnschools.gov.in are JavaScript apps that returned no content, and the sandbox shell has no internet access. Because of this every chapter is marked verified:false. Chapter titles were cross-checked between two independent secondary sites (Shaalaa and Brainkart), which agree on every chapter title and order. Neither is official.

Edition currency for 2026-27: DT Next (8 May 2026; 16 Aug 2026) reports that only Classes 1-3 received new-syllabus books in 2026-27. Classes 4-12 continue on the existing Samacheer Kalvi syllabus (the 2018-19 / 2019-20 'new syllabus' books), and the new State Education Policy curriculum is targeted for 2027-28. The same article says Classes 4-12 books with the old syllabus were 'being prepared' for 2026-27, so a 2026 reprint or re-typeset printing may exist. I could not see its imprint page to confirm the edition line or any content changes.

Section titles come from Brainkart's topic index for this book, which follows the textbook's headings. They were not checked against the official PDF. I dropped exercise, summary, 'Try these' and worked-example entries and kept only content headings. Section ids are positional, not the textbook's own section numbers, which I could not see.
All outcomes are my own paraphrases of chapter content; no textbook text is reproduced.
Competencies listed under 'proposed' are reused across the TN Grade 6, 7 and 8 files with identical ids and definitions.

Grade 7 is published as three term books. Each term restarts chapter numbering at 1, so the ids encode the term (tn-g07-t2-c03 ...). For 2026-27 the term structure still holds: the proposal to merge the Class 6-7 books into one volume targets 2027-28 (DT Next, Aug 2026).

Exercise counts from Shaalaa match Brainkart's index for every Grade 7 chapter, which suggests both follow the same printing. The one exception is T3 Information Processing, where both list only Exercise 6.1 (flowcharts).

T3 Algebra 'Inequations' covers simple one-variable inequations at an introductory level. I mapped it as a partial fit to MATH.algebra.inequalities, which the list places at Grade 11, rather than proposing a near-duplicate.

T2 Information Processing 'Pascal's Triangle': Brainkart writes 'Pascal s Triangle'; I restored the apostrophe. T1 Geometry 'special angles without protractor' presumably means 60, 30, 90, 45 and 120 degrees; I could not confirm the exact list.

sections.title: Distributive Property of Multiplication over Addition
Statement Problems on Integers using all Fundamental Operations

outcomes.statement: Add and subtract integers, using the number line and sign rules.
Multiply and divide integers using the sign rules.

competencies.why: Multiplying integers by the sign rules is ajimul and dividing integers is the new ajidiv, both in integer-multiply; the outcome is mapped only to rational-numbers.

outcomes.statement: Check which properties (closure, commutative, associative, identity, distributive) hold for each integer operation, using counterexamples where a property fails.

proposed.name: Use closure, commutative, associative, distributive and identity properties of operations on a number system
proposed.why: Existing list has only MLY.alg.distributive (one property, algebraic); TN teaches the property set explicitly for whole numbers (G6), integers (G7) and rationals (G8).

outcomes.statement: Solve word problems that need several integer operations, such as temperature changes, depths or scores.

sections.title: Area and Perimeter of the Parallelogram

outcomes.statement: Calculate the area and perimeter of a parallelogram from its base, height and sides, and find a missing dimension.

proposed.name: Calculate area and perimeter of parallelograms and rhombuses (base-height and diagonal formulas)
proposed.why: The list jumps from triangle area (G6) to trapezium/composite areas (G8); parallelogram and rhombus area formulas have no home.

outcomes.statement: Calculate the area of a rhombus from its diagonals and use it to find an unknown diagonal.

proposed.name: Calculate area and perimeter of parallelograms and rhombuses (base-height and diagonal formulas)
proposed.why: The list jumps from triangle area (G6) to trapezium/composite areas (G8); parallelogram and rhombus area formulas have no home.

outcomes.statement: Calculate the area of a trapezium from its parallel sides and height, including in field and plot problems.

sections.title: Addition and Subtraction of Algebraic expressions

outcomes.statement: Identify the terms, coefficients and constants of an expression, and tell like terms from unlike terms.
Evaluate an algebraic expression for given values of its variables.
Add and subtract algebraic expressions by combining like terms.
Form and solve simple linear equations in one variable from word problems.
Recognise when two quantities vary directly and solve direct-proportion problems with the unitary method or a ratio.
Recognise when two quantities vary inversely and solve problems about workers and time or speed and time.
Decide from a table or situation whether a relationship is direct, inverse or neither.

sections.title: Pair of Angles formed by Intersecting Lines
Construction of perpendicular bisector of a line segment
Construction of angle bisector of an angle
Construction of special angles without using protractor

outcomes.statement: Use adjacent angles, linear pairs and vertically opposite angles at intersecting lines to find unknown angles.

proposed.name: Identify and use complementary, supplementary, adjacent, linear-pair and vertically opposite angles
proposed.why: parallel-angles covers transversal angles only; angle-pair relationships without parallel lines are not in the list.

outcomes.statement: Identify the corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles formed by a transversal, and use them to find angles or test lines for parallelism.
Construct the perpendicular bisector of a line segment and the bisector of an angle with ruler and compass.
Construct special angles such as 60, 30, 90, 45 and 120 degrees with ruler and compass only.
Fit tetromino shapes together to tile or fill a given region.
Read a route map to describe paths with directions and choose the shortest or most suitable route.

competencies.why: The new route families (paths described with directions and a scale; the shortest route through a road table) and the written route task wr:map-route-choose are in maps-directions, which this outcome (mapped to positions and multi-step) does not list.

sections.title: Representing Decimal Numbers on the Number Line

outcomes.statement: Represent decimals in place-value form, expanded form and with tenths/hundredths models.
Convert fractions to decimals and decimals to fractions in simplest form.
Compare and order decimal numbers.
Locate decimal numbers on a number line.
Name the parts of a circle and relate radius and diameter.
Calculate the circumference of a circle and find the radius from a given circumference, including distance-by-wheel problems.
Calculate the area of a circle, and of rings and semicircles.
Find the area of rectangular and circular pathways by subtracting inner areas from outer areas.

sections.title: Unit Digit of Numbers in Exponential Form

outcomes.statement: Write repeated products in exponential form and evaluate powers, including expressing a number as a product of prime powers.

competencies.why: Expressing a number as a product of primes is asked by ajpf; the prime-power (index) form is the new avppf in the mapped exponents competency.

outcomes.statement: Apply the product, quotient, power-of-a-power and zero-exponent laws to simplify expressions.
Find the unit digit of a large power using the repeating cycle of unit digits.
Determine the degree of a monomial or polynomial expression.

sections.title: Application of Angle Sum Property of Triangle

outcomes.statement: Use the angle-sum property and the exterior-angle property to find unknown angles of triangles.
Identify corresponding parts of congruent figures and use the SSS, SAS, ASA and RHS criteria to decide whether two triangles are congruent.

sections.title: Tables and Patterns Leading to Linear Functions

outcomes.statement: Find the linear rule linking two quantities from a table of values and use it to predict new values.
Build Pascal's triangle and describe the number patterns in its rows and diagonals.

sections.title: Addition and Subtraction of Decimal Numbers

outcomes.statement: Round decimals to the nearest whole number, tenth or hundredth.

proposed.name: Round whole numbers and decimals to a given place and use rounding to estimate
proposed.why: MATH.reasoning.estimate-check is about checking answers; no competency covers the place-value rounding procedure itself.

outcomes.statement: Add and subtract decimal numbers, including in money and measurement problems.
Multiply decimals by whole numbers, by powers of 10 and by other decimals.
Divide decimals by whole numbers, by powers of 10 and by other decimals, and solve related word problems.
Convert between fractions, decimals and percentages.
Calculate a percentage of a quantity and express one quantity as a percentage of another in real-life situations such as marks, populations or discounts.
Calculate simple interest, amount, principal, rate or time when the other quantities are given.

sections.title: Geometrical Approach to Multiplication of Monomials

outcomes.statement: Use area models to multiply monomials and binomials.
Verify the identities for (a+b)^2, (a-b)^2 and (a+b)(a-b) with area diagrams and use them to expand expressions.
Factorise expressions that match a standard identity.
Solve simple one-variable inequations over whole numbers or integers and show the solution set on a number line.

sections.title: Construction of circles and concentric circles

outcomes.statement: Apply reflections, translations and rotations to figures and identify the symmetry each transformation produces.

proposed.name: Perform and describe reflections, translations and rotations of figures
proposed.why: No competency covers rigid transformations as operations on figures.

proposed.name: Identify rotational symmetry and its order (and translational symmetry in patterns)
proposed.why: Existing symmetry competencies are reflection/line symmetry only.

outcomes.statement: Construct circles and concentric circles from given radii, or from a given ring width, using a compass.
Collect and organise data into tables.
Calculate the arithmetic mean of a data set and interpret it as a representative value.
Find the mode and median of ungrouped data and choose an appropriate representative value.
Read a flowchart that uses the standard symbols and trace it to find the output.
